subject: Finalizing commit bands & reconciliation cadence for Hosted API pricing

Subject: Hosted API commit bands — initial ask

Hi Michael,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to get our buying team on a clear commit band proposal and to lock down how quarterly true-ups will work. We have two main asks: a) a clear sliding scale of per-token discounts by committed monthly volume bands, and b) a simple reconciliation flow so we can forecast cashflows for FY28.

We reviewed the spreadsheet you sent (v2); attached is a quick markup with our preferred bands and a suggested annual true-up instead of quarterly (we may be able to commit more seasonally). Can you confirm whether you can support:
- make-goods delivered as one-off credits applied to the following invoice or a lump-sum credit at year-end
- an option to allow temporary burst usage beyond committed tiers billed at a capped overage rate

We're aiming to finalize terms by the end of next week so finance can approve.

Attachment: Acme_markups_v1.xlsx (7 KB)

Best,
Jill Park

Subject: Re: Hosted API commit bands — initial ask

Jill — thanks for the clear notes and the markup. High level responses below, then I loop Rishi for the reconciliation mechanics.

1) Commit bands: we can support tiered per-token pricing with monthly commit tiers. For your markup, the effective blended price at the bands you proposed looks reasonable; we pushed a cleaned version (attached) with an alternate band that smooths the breakpoint at 10M tokens.
2) Make-goods / credits: we offer two mutually-agreeable flows: 
   - Quarterly true-up with make-goods (credit applied on the next invoice); or
   - Annual true-up with a single settlement credit or charge at year-end.

We typically recommend quarterly true-ups for younger customers so surprises are limited, but annual works if your finance team prefers it. Bursting: yes — overages billed at a capped premium (we can cap at +30% of committed per-token in your case).

I've attached a fresh workbook (Redwood_Commit_Bands_v3.xlsx) with the capped overage line and example settlement calculations for both quarterly and annual flows.

Next steps: if you prefer annual true-up, confirm and we'll draft contract language that describes the settlement mechanics and timing. If quarterly, Rishi (cc'd) will propose an operational playbook for invoicing and credits.

Attachment: Redwood_Commit_Bands_v3.xlsx (24 KB)

Thanks,

Hi all — happy to lay out the reconciliation playbook for quarterly vs annual so procurement and finance can pick. Short version below plus the operational checklist.

Quarterly true-up (recommended for visibility):
- At the start of each quarter we estimate expected consumption based on trailing 3 months (forecast only).
- At quarter close we compute actual usage for that quarter versus committed (commit is based on monthly equivalent).
- If usage < commit, no make-good is issued; your credits do not roll forward.
- If usage > commit, Redwood issues a make-good credit equal to the delta priced at the committed band rate (not the overage rate) OR invoices the overage at the capped overage rate depending on contract choice.
- Make-goods are applied as a credit on the next invoice; refunds are not typical.

Annual true-up (simpler cash ops):
- We aggregate actual usage over the 12-month term against the annual committed tokens.
- If under-committed, no refund; if over, either a single invoice for the overage at the capped rate or a credit applied at next term start.

Operational checklist for either flow:
- HubSpot deal field populated with committed monthly tokens + chosen true-up cadence.
- Invoice notes include: committed tier id, measurement window, and cap on overage rate.
- Finance must accept credit application flow (credit vs invoice).
- DocuSign clause: one paragraph that defines measurement, rounding (we use token granularity), and dispute window (30 days).

I attached a one-page sample invoice note and example calculation for both flows. If you want, we can run a blind example for April-June to show the numbers.

Attachment: Quarterly_vs_Annual_Playbook.pdf (12 KB)

-Rishi
